title: Variance and influence inequality
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$. With expectation taken uniformly on the cube, let $\mathrm{Inf}(g)$ be the sum of its coordinate influences and let $W_1(g)=\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat g(S)^2$ be its Fourier weight at level one. Then $2\bigl(\mathbb E[g^2]-(\mathbb E g)^2\bigr)\le \mathrm{Inf}(g)+W_1(g)$.
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and equip $\{0,1\}^n$ with its uniform probability measure; write $\mathbb E$ for uniform expectation. For $S\subseteq[n]$, put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for real cube functions $h$. Write $x^{\{i\}}$ for $x$ with bit $i$ flipped, $I_i(h)=\mathbb E[(h(x)-h(x^{\{i\}}))^2]/4$, and $I(h)=\sum_i I_i(h)$. For every real cube function $g$, $2(\mathbb E[g^2]-(\mathbb Eg)^2)\le I(g)+\sum_{|S|=1}\widehat g(S)^2$.
